page: Microsoft Azure ND96amsr_A100_v4 is an x86_64 GPU-accelerated virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The compute foundation consists of 96 dedicated AMD vCPUs backed by 1800.0 GB of system memory, providing a high allocation of 18.75 GB RAM per core. This configuration prioritizes hardware resource density for heavy in-memory operations and parallel computations.

Hardware acceleration is delivered via eight integrated NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs, providing an aggregate of 640 GB of VRAM. For I/O and low-latency data access, the instance includes 10,794 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. The server is also RDMA capable to support distributed computing across nodes and supports Azure Premium Storage.

Given the density of eight A100 GPUs alongside extensive host memory and multi-terabyte NVMe storage, this server minimizes host-to-accelerator bottlenecks. It is designed for large-scale distributed artificial intelligence workloads, deep learning model training, massive LLM inference, and high-performance scientific simulations.
